changes.text: 1783年12月22日，星期一，大陆会议议定了第二天公开接见总司令华盛顿将军的次序。一个统帅军队的人要当众把受托的权力交回一个坐着开会的机构；这个场面里谁坐着、谁站着、谁鞠躬、谁脱帽，国会都逐条写进了日志。

On Monday, 22 December 1783, the Continental Congress settled the order of the next day's public audience with its commander-in-chief, General Washington. A man who had commanded armies was about to hand delegated power back, in public, to a body that did its business sitting down. Who would sit, who would stand, who would bow and who would lift a hat: Congress wrote each of these into its journal.

说完，他走上前，把委任状和讲稿副本一并交给议长。委任状是权力的凭证，副本是这番说法的书面文本，两件东西一次交清。议定稿这一步留有方括号改动的痕迹，日志记下的结果是：由他本人走上前，交到议长手里。仪式并没有在交接处结束：按议定次序，接下来由议长宣读国会的答词，将军站着听；日志随后载有这篇答词。答词开头说，合众国国会怀着难以言表的感情接受他交还的权力；后半部分还回应了他的请求，表示国会将特别负责照顾那些一直随侍在他身边的亲信军官的利益。

With that, he stepped forward and placed his commission, together with a copy of his address, in the President's hands. The journal records it in one line: "He then advanced and delivered to the President his commission, with a copy of his address". The commission was the token of authority; the copy was the written text of what he had said. Two objects, delivered at once. The draft at this step carries bracketed changes; what the journal records is that he himself stepped forward and put the commission into the President's hands. The ceremony did not end with the handover. Under the agreed order, the President was next to deliver the answer of Congress, which the General was to receive standing, and the journal goes on to print that answer. It opens by saying that the United States in Congress assembled "receive with emotions, too affecting for utterance" the return of his authority; later it answers his request about his officers, saying Congress "will particularly charge ourselves with the interests of those confidential officers" who had attended him.

作者推断，这套流程的要害在于它不依赖任何人相信谁的品格：仪式前一日成文，次日按议定次序进行，凭证当场易手，讲稿副本随凭证一并交出。（据日志，委任状是交给议长的；议定稿第4条经方括号增字后，也写明把委任状和讲稿副本交给议长，与日志所记一致。第6条仍有由秘书接收委任状的字样，但本篇所据的OCR文本在这一处有乱码，无法判断这些字是否已被删去。）一个人是否忠诚，一场仪式无法证明；但权力是否已归位，可以在这一天被记成白纸黑字。这是作者对记录方式的解释，日志本身并未陈述其用意。

The author's inference is that the point of the procedure was that it depended on nobody's character. The order was written the day before and followed the next day, the token changed hands on the spot, and a copy of the address was handed over along with it. (The journal has the commission delivered to the President. Clause 4 of the draft, as amended by the bracketed insertions, also has the commission and the copy of the address going to the President, which matches the journal. Clause 6 still contains wording in which the secretary receives the commission, but the OCR text this piece relies on is garbled at that point and cannot show whether those words were struck out.) A man's loyalty cannot be proven by a ceremony. Whether power has been put back where it belongs, however, can be entered in black and white on a particular day. That is an interpretation of how the record was made; the journal itself states no such intention.

本篇所据只有《大陆会议日志》第25卷的官方记录：12月20日至23日的记录，包括12月22日议定的接见次序、23日的接见经过与讲话文本。没有取得任何在场者的私人记述，因此讲话者的神情与语气、在场个人的现场反应，本篇都无从得知。日志记动作、记次序、记讲话，不描写个人的神情与现场反应。讲话本身说到他对独立得到确认感到欣慰、高兴，国会的正式答词也自称怀着难以言表的感情接受，但这些是写成文字的正式表态，答词更是机构的书面表态，不是对现场的描写。本篇也不涉及他此后的事。凡是原文没写的动机、念头和“他考虑过的选项”，本篇都不替他补。

Everything in this piece rests on one source: the official Journals of the Continental Congress, volume 25 — the record of December 20 to 23, including the order of audience agreed on December 22, the audience of the twenty-third, and the text of the address. No private account by anyone present was consulted, and so the speaker's face and tone, and the reactions of individuals in the room, are beyond what this piece can know. The journal records gestures, sequence, and speech; it does not describe individual faces or reactions in the room. The address itself speaks of being "Happy" and "pleased", and Congress's formal answer says it receives "with emotions, too affecting for utterance", but these are formal statements set down in writing, the answer being the institution's own written statement, not descriptions of the scene. Nor does this piece follow the man beyond that day. Motives, private thoughts, and options he may have considered are never supplied by this writer where the source is silent.
另有三处技术性保留。第一，国会的答词见于日志，本篇只引用其中OCR清晰的片段。第二，这份材料取自影印本的OCR识别，存在讹字，本篇英文引文只取清晰片段，可疑拼写一律留在引号之外。第三，日志印本以方括号标出议定稿中的改动字样，据编者注，方括号里的字出自博迪诺之手；本篇所据的OCR文本无法判断原稿另有哪些删改，本篇只转述方括号中的字样。

Three technical reservations follow. First, Congress's answer appears in the journal, and this piece quotes only the stretches of it that the OCR renders cleanly. Second, the material comes from OCR of a facsimile and contains misreadings, so the English quotations here take only clean stretches, with doubtful spellings left outside the quotation marks. Third, the printed journal marks changes to the draft protocol with brackets, and according to the editors' note the bracketed words are in Boudinot's writing; the OCR text this piece relies on cannot show whether the draft carries any other deletions or revisions, so this piece reports only what is in the brackets.

全部事实来自《大陆会议日志》第25卷的官方记录（1783年12月20日的来信、议决与关于七州权限的表决，12月22日议定的接见次序，12月23日的接见、华盛顿讲话文本与国会答词）。没有在场者私人记述可对照，个人神情与现场反应不可知；国会的正式答词见于日志，本篇只按OCR清晰的片段引用；带括号改动的是接见次序的议定稿；材料经OCR识别，存在讹字，引文只取清晰片段；议定稿的改动在本篇所据的OCR文本中只能确认方括号内的字样（据编者注为博迪诺笔迹），其他删改无法判断。

All facts come from the official Journals of the Continental Congress, volume 25 (the letter, resolution and vote on whether seven states were competent, of December 20, 1783; the order of audience agreed on December 22; the audience, Washington's address and Congress's answer of December 23). No private account by anyone present was available for comparison, so individual faces and reactions in the room are unknowable; Congress's formal answer appears in the journal and is quoted here only in clean stretches; the draft bearing bracketed changes is the protocol of the order of audience; the material was captured by OCR from a facsimile and contains misreadings, so quotations take only clean stretches; in the draft protocol, the OCR text this piece relies on confirms only the bracketed words (in Boudinot's writing, according to the editors' note), and any other deletions or revisions cannot be determined.
